The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

53	/// A pull based CSV reader.
54	///
55	/// This reader parses CSV data using a finite state machine. Callers can
56	/// extract parsed data incrementally using one of the `read` methods.
57	///
58	/// Note that this CSV reader is somewhat encoding agnostic. The source data
59	/// needs to be at least ASCII compatible. There is no support for specifying
60	/// the full gamut of Unicode delimiters/terminators/quotes/escapes. Instead,
61	/// any byte can be used, although callers probably want to stick to the ASCII
62	/// subset (`<= 0x7F`).
63	///
64	/// # Usage
65	///
66	/// A reader has two different ways to read CSV data, each with their own
67	/// trade offs.
68	///
69	/// * `read_field` - Copies a single CSV field into an output buffer while
70	///   unescaping quotes. This is simple to use and doesn't require storing an
71	///   entire record contiguously in memory, but it is slower.
72	/// * `read_record` - Copies an entire CSV record into an output buffer while
73	///   unescaping quotes. The ending positions of each field are copied into
74	///   an additional buffer. This is harder to use and requires larger output
75	///   buffers, but it is faster than `read_field` since it amortizes more
76	///   costs.
77	///
78	/// # RFC 4180
79	///
80	/// [RFC 4180](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4180)
81	/// is the closest thing to a specification for CSV data. Unfortunately,
82	/// CSV data that is seen in the wild can vary significantly. Often, the CSV
83	/// data is outright invalid. Instead of fixing the producers of bad CSV data,
84	/// we have seen fit to make consumers much more flexible in what they accept.
85	/// This reader continues that tradition, and therefore, isn't technically
86	/// compliant with RFC 4180. In particular, this reader will never return an
87	/// error and will always find *a* parse.
88	///
89	/// Here are some detailed differences from RFC 4180:
90	///
91	/// * CRLF, LF and CR are each treated as a single record terminator by
92	///   default.
93	/// * Records are permitted to be of varying length.
94	/// * Empty lines (that do not include other whitespace) are ignored.
95	#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
96	pub struct Reader {
97	    /// A table-based DFA for parsing CSV.
98	    dfa: Dfa,
99	    /// The current DFA state, if the DFA is used.
100	    dfa_state: DfaState,
101	    /// The current NFA state, if the NFA is used.
102	    nfa_state: NfaState,
103	    /// The delimiter that separates fields.
104	    delimiter: u8,
105	    /// The terminator that separates records.
106	    term: Terminator,
107	    /// The quotation byte.
108	    quote: u8,
109	    /// Whether to recognize escaped quotes.
110	    escape: Option<u8>,
111	    /// Whether to recognized doubled quotes.
112	    double_quote: bool,
113	    /// If enabled, lines beginning with this byte are ignored.
114	    comment: Option<u8>,
115	    /// If enabled (the default), then quotes are respected. When disabled,
116	    /// quotes are not treated specially.
117	    quoting: bool,
118	    /// Whether to use the NFA for parsing.
119	    ///
120	    /// Generally this is for debugging. There's otherwise no good reason
121	    /// to avoid the DFA.
122	    use_nfa: bool,
123	    /// The current line number.
124	    line: u64,
125	    /// The state of UTF-8 BOM detection at the start of the stream.
126	    bom: Bom,
127	    /// The current position in the output buffer when reading a record.
128	    output_pos: usize,
129	}
130	
131	/// The bytes of a UTF-8 byte order mark.
132	const BOM: [u8; 3] = [0xEF, 0xBB, 0xBF];
133	
134	/// The phase of UTF-8 BOM detection at the start of a stream.
135	///
136	/// A BOM is only recognized when it is the first thing in a stream, so
137	/// detection is active only for a fresh reader (or after a call to `reset`).
138	/// The BOM may arrive split across several caller-provided buffers, so the
139	/// detector remembers any unmatched prefix. If the BOM is ruled out (either
140	/// because a byte does not match or because the stream ended early), the
141	/// candidate bytes are fed to the parser as ordinary data instead of being
142	/// swallowed.
143	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
144	enum Bom {
145	    /// Detection is in progress and `0`, `1` or `2` leading BOM bytes have
146	    /// been observed and held back from the parser.
147	    Check(u8),
148	    /// The BOM was ruled out and the held candidate bytes, a slice of
149	    /// `BOM[start..end]`, still need to be replayed to the parser as ordinary
150	    /// data.
151	    Replay(u8, u8),
152	    /// BOM detection has finished (the BOM was found and removed, it was
153	    /// ruled out, detection was disabled, or all held bytes were replayed).
154	    Done,
155	}
156	
157	/// The outcome of advancing BOM detection over one caller chunk.
158	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
159	enum BomStep {
160	    /// Every byte of the chunk extended the still-incomplete BOM candidate;
161	    /// they were absorbed and must not reach the parser yet.
162	    Hold,
163	    /// A complete BOM was formed using this many bytes of the chunk; those
164	    /// bytes are removed.
165	    Strip(usize),
166	    /// A byte did not match the BOM. The first `consumed` bytes of the chunk
167	    /// (together with bytes held by earlier reads) are ordinary data queued
168	    /// for replay; the mismatch byte and everything after it remain in the
169	    /// caller's input.
170	    Mismatch { consumed: usize },
171	}

327	impl ReadFieldResult {
328	    fn from_nfa(
329	        state: NfaState,
330	        inpdone: bool,
331	        outdone: bool,
332	    ) -> ReadFieldResult {
333	        match state {
334	            NfaState::End => ReadFieldResult::End,

453	/// An NFA state is a state that can be visited in the NFA parser.
454	///
455	/// Given the simplicity of the machine, a subset of NFA states double as DFA
456	/// states. NFA states that only have incoming epsilon transitions are
457	/// optimized out when converting the machine to a DFA.

459	enum NfaState {
460	    // These states aren't used in the DFA, so we
461	    // assign them meaningless numbers.
462	    EndFieldTerm = 200,
463	    InRecordTerm = 201,
464	    End = 202,
465	
466	    // All states below are DFA states.
467	    StartRecord = 0,
468	    StartField = 1,
469	    InField = 2,
470	    InQuotedField = 3,
471	    InEscapedQuote = 4,
472	    InDoubleEscapedQuote = 5,
473	    InComment = 6,
474	    // All states below are "final field" states.
475	    // Namely, they indicate that a field has been parsed.
476	    EndFieldDelim = 7,
477	    // All states below are "final record" states.
478	    // Namely, they indicate that a record has been parsed.
479	    EndRecord = 8,
480	    CRLF = 9,
481	}

483	/// A list of NFA states that have an explicit representation in the DFA.
484	const NFA_STATES: &[NfaState] = &[
485	    NfaState::StartRecord,
486	    NfaState::StartField,
487	    NfaState::EndFieldDelim,
488	    NfaState::InField,
489	    NfaState::InQuotedField,
490	    NfaState::InEscapedQuote,
491	    NfaState::InDoubleEscapedQuote,
492	    NfaState::InComment,
493	    NfaState::EndRecord,
494	    NfaState::CRLF,
495	];

497	impl NfaState {
498	    /// Returns true if this state indicates that a field has been parsed.
499	    fn is_field_final(&self) -> bool {
500	        matches!(
501	            *self,
502	            NfaState::End
503	                | NfaState::EndRecord
504	                | NfaState::CRLF
505	                | NfaState::EndFieldDelim
506	        )
507	    }

509	    /// Returns true if this state indicates that a record has been parsed.
510	    fn is_record_final(&self) -> bool {
511	        matches!(*self, NfaState::End | NfaState::EndRecord | NfaState::CRLF)

562	    /// Parse a single CSV field in `input` and copy field data to `output`.
563	    ///
564	    /// This routine requires a caller provided buffer of CSV data as the
565	    /// `input` and a caller provided buffer, `output`, in which to store field
566	    /// data extracted from `input`. The field data copied to `output` will
567	    /// have its quotes unescaped.
568	    ///
569	    /// Calling this routine parses at most a single field and returns
570	    /// three values indicating the state of the parser. The first value, a
571	    /// `ReadFieldResult`, tells the caller what to do next. For example, if
572	    /// the entire input was read or if the output buffer was filled before
573	    /// a full field had been read, then `ReadFieldResult::InputEmpty` or
574	    /// `ReadFieldResult::OutputFull` is returned, respectively. See the
575	    /// documentation for `ReadFieldResult` for more details.
576	    ///
577	    /// The other two values returned correspond to the number of bytes
578	    /// read from `input` and written to `output`, respectively.
579	    ///
580	    /// # Termination
581	    ///
582	    /// This reader interprets an empty `input` buffer as an indication that
583	    /// there is no CSV data left to read. Namely, when the caller has
584	    /// exhausted all CSV data, the caller should continue to call `read` with
585	    /// an empty input buffer until `ReadFieldResult::End` is returned.
586	    ///
587	    /// # Errors
588	    ///
589	    /// This CSV reader can never return an error. Instead, it prefers *a*
590	    /// parse over *no* parse.
591	    pub fn read_field(
592	        &mut self,
593	        input: &[u8],
594	        output: &mut [u8],
595	    ) -> (ReadFieldResult, usize, usize) {
596	        let mut nin = 0;
597	        let mut nout = 0;
598	        // `data` is the caller input that reaches the parser once BOM
599	        // detection is accounted for.
600	        let mut data: &[u8] = input;
601	        if let Bom::Check(held) = self.bom {
602	            if input.is_empty() {
603	                // End of stream: a held prefix is ordinary data, not a BOM.
604	                self.bom =
605	                    if held == 0 { Bom::Done } else { Bom::Replay(0, held) };
606	            } else {
607	                match self.bom_detect(input) {
608	                    // The whole chunk is an undecided prefix of the BOM.
609	                    BomStep::Hold => {
610	                        return (ReadFieldResult::InputEmpty, input.len(), 0)
611	                    }
612	                    // A complete BOM ended within this chunk.
613	                    BomStep::Strip(skip) => {
614	                        nin = skip;
615	                        data = &input[skip..];
616	                    }
617	                    // A byte ruled the BOM out. The candidate bytes (the held
618	                    // prefix followed by this call's matching run) are queued
619	                    // for replay; the rest of the chunk is ordinary data.
620	                    BomStep::Mismatch { consumed } => {
621	                        nin = consumed;
622	                        data = &input[consumed..];
623	                    }
624	                }
625	            }
626	        }
627	        // Replay candidate bytes now known not to be a BOM. They never count
628	        // toward `nin` of this call.
629	        if let Bom::Replay(a, b) = self.bom {
630	            let (mut start, end) = (a as usize, b as usize);
631	            loop {
632	                if start >= end {
633	                    self.bom = Bom::Done;
634	                    break;
635	                }
636	                let (res, rn, on) = self
637	                    .read_field_once(&BOM[start..end], &mut output[nout..]);
638	                start += rn;
639	                nout += on;
640	                match res {
641	                    ReadFieldResult::InputEmpty => continue,
642	                    _ => {
643	                        self.bom = Bom::Replay(start as u8, end as u8);
644	                        return (res, nin, nout);
645	                    }
646	                }
647	            }
648	        }
649	        // A non-empty chunk that consisted of exactly the confirmed BOM
650	        // produces an empty data slice but must not trigger the final
651	        // transition; the caller signals real end of stream with an empty
652	        // input.
653	        if !input.is_empty() && data.is_empty() {
654	            return (ReadFieldResult::InputEmpty, nin, nout);
655	        }
656	        let (res, rn, on) = self.read_field_once(data, &mut output[nout..]);
657	        (res, nin + rn, nout + on)
658	    }
659	
660	    /// Dispatch a single chunk to either the NFA or DFA field parser.
661	    #[inline(always)]
662	    fn read_field_once(
663	        &mut self,
664	        input: &[u8],
665	        output: &mut [u8],
666	    ) -> (ReadFieldResult, usize, usize) {
667	        if self.use_nfa {
668	            self.read_field_nfa(input, output)
669	        } else {
670	            self.read_field_dfa(input, output)
671	        }
672	    }

674	    /// Parse a single CSV record in `input` and copy each field contiguously
675	    /// to `output`, with the end position of each field written to `ends`.
676	    ///
677	    /// **NOTE**: This method is more cumbersome to use than `read_field`, but
678	    /// it can be faster since it amortizes more work.
679	    ///
680	    /// This routine requires a caller provided buffer of CSV data as the
681	    /// `input` and two caller provided buffers to store the unescaped field
682	    /// data (`output`) and the end position of each field in the record
683	    /// (`fields`).
684	    ///
685	    /// Calling this routine parses at most a single record and returns four
686	    /// values indicating the state of the parser. The first value, a
687	    /// `ReadRecordResult`, tells the caller what to do next. For example, if
688	    /// the entire input was read or if the output buffer was filled before a
689	    /// full field had been read, then `ReadRecordResult::InputEmpty` or
690	    /// `ReadRecordResult::OutputFull` is returned, respectively. Similarly, if
691	    /// the `ends` buffer is full, then `ReadRecordResult::OutputEndsFull` is
692	    /// returned. See the documentation for `ReadRecordResult` for more
693	    /// details.
694	    ///
695	    /// The other three values correspond to the number of bytes read from
696	    /// `input`, the number of bytes written to `output` and the number of
697	    /// end positions written to `ends`, respectively.
698	    ///
699	    /// The end positions written to `ends` are constructed as if there was
700	    /// a single contiguous buffer in memory containing the entire row, even
701	    /// if `ReadRecordResult::OutputFull` was returned in the middle of reading
702	    /// a row.
703	    ///
704	    /// # Termination
705	    ///
706	    /// This reader interprets an empty `input` buffer as an indication that
707	    /// there is no CSV data left to read. Namely, when the caller has
708	    /// exhausted all CSV data, the caller should continue to call `read` with
709	    /// an empty input buffer until `ReadRecordResult::End` is returned.
710	    ///
711	    /// # Errors
712	    ///
713	    /// This CSV reader can never return an error. Instead, it prefers *a*
714	    /// parse over *no* parse.
715	    pub fn read_record(
716	        &mut self,
717	        input: &[u8],
718	        output: &mut [u8],
719	        ends: &mut [usize],
720	    ) -> (ReadRecordResult, usize, usize, usize) {
721	        let mut nin = 0;
722	        let mut nout = 0;
723	        let mut nend = 0;
724	        // `data` is the caller input that reaches the parser once BOM
725	        // detection is accounted for.
726	        let mut data: &[u8] = input;
727	        if let Bom::Check(held) = self.bom {
728	            if input.is_empty() {
729	                // End of stream: a held prefix is ordinary data, not a BOM.
730	                self.bom =
731	                    if held == 0 { Bom::Done } else { Bom::Replay(0, held) };
732	            } else {
733	                match self.bom_detect(input) {
734	                    // The whole chunk is an undecided prefix of the BOM.
735	                    BomStep::Hold => {
736	                        return (
737	                            ReadRecordResult::InputEmpty,
738	                            input.len(),
739	                            0,
740	                            0,
741	                        )
742	                    }
743	                    // A complete BOM ended within this chunk.
744	                    BomStep::Strip(skip) => {
745	                        nin = skip;
746	                        data = &input[skip..];
747	                    }
748	                    // A byte ruled the BOM out. The candidate bytes are queued
749	                    // for replay; the rest of the chunk is ordinary data.
750	                    BomStep::Mismatch { consumed } => {
751	                        nin = consumed;
752	                        data = &input[consumed..];
753	                    }
754	                }
755	            }
756	        }
757	        // Replay candidate bytes now known not to be a BOM. They never count
758	        // toward `nin` of this call.
759	        if let Bom::Replay(a, b) = self.bom {
760	            let (mut start, end) = (a as usize, b as usize);
761	            loop {
762	                if start >= end {
763	                    self.bom = Bom::Done;
764	                    break;
765	                }
766	                let (res, rn, on, en) = self.read_record_once(
767	                    &BOM[start..end],
768	                    &mut output[nout..],
769	                    &mut ends[nend..],
770	                );
771	                start += rn;
772	                nout += on;
773	                nend += en;
774	                match res {
775	                    ReadRecordResult::InputEmpty => continue,
776	                    _ => {
777	                        self.bom = Bom::Replay(start as u8, end as u8);
778	                        return (res, nin, nout, nend);
779	                    }
780	                }
781	            }
782	        }
783	        // A non-empty chunk that consisted of exactly the confirmed BOM
784	        // produces an empty data slice but must not trigger the final
785	        // transition; the caller signals real end of stream with an empty
786	        // input.
787	        if !input.is_empty() && data.is_empty() {
788	            return (ReadRecordResult::InputEmpty, nin, nout, nend);
789	        }
790	        let (res, rn, on, en) = self.read_record_once(
791	            data,
792	            &mut output[nout..],
793	            &mut ends[nend..],
794	        );
795	        (res, nin + rn, nout + on, nend + en)
796	    }

798	    /// Dispatch a single chunk to either the NFA or DFA record parser.
799	    #[inline(always)]
800	    fn read_record_once(
801	        &mut self,
802	        input: &[u8],
803	        output: &mut [u8],
804	        ends: &mut [usize],
805	    ) -> (ReadRecordResult, usize, usize, usize) {
806	        if self.use_nfa {
807	            self.read_record_nfa(input, output, ends)
808	        } else {
809	            self.read_record_dfa(input, output, ends)
810	        }
811	    }

813	    /// Advance BOM detection over the caller's chunk.
814	    ///
815	    /// On entry `self.bom` is `Bom::Check(held)` with `held` candidate bytes
816	    /// already absorbed from earlier reads, and `input` is non-empty. The
817	    /// returned step describes what happened:
818	    ///
819	    /// * `Hold` — every byte of `input` extends the candidate prefix, which is
820	    ///   still shorter than the BOM. All bytes are consumed.
821	    /// * `Strip(n)` — the candidate plus the first `n` bytes is the complete
822	    ///   BOM. Those `n` bytes are consumed and removed.
823	    /// * `Mismatch { consumed }` — `input[consumed]` is the first byte that
824	    ///   does not match. The `consumed` matching bytes, together with the
825	    ///   previously held prefix, are queued in `Bom::Replay` and must be fed
826	    ///   back to the parser as ordinary data; the mismatch byte and the rest
827	    ///   of the chunk stay in the caller's input.
828	    #[inline(always)]
829	    fn bom_detect(&mut self, input: &[u8]) -> BomStep {
830	        let held = match self.bom {
831	            Bom::Check(h) => h as usize,
832	            _ => unreachable!(),
833	        };
834	        let mut i = 0;
835	        while held + i < BOM.len()
836	            && i < input.len()
837	            && input[i] == BOM[held + i]
838	        {
839	            i += 1;
840	        }
841	        let matched = held + i;
842	        if matched == BOM.len() {
843	            self.bom = Bom::Done;
844	            BomStep::Strip(i)
845	        } else if i == input.len() {
846	            self.bom = Bom::Check(matched as u8);
847	            BomStep::Hold
848	        } else if matched == 0 {
849	            // The very first byte rules the BOM out; nothing to replay.
850	            self.bom = Bom::Done;
851	            BomStep::Mismatch { consumed: 0 }
852	        } else {
853	            self.bom = Bom::Replay(0, matched as u8);
854	            BomStep::Mismatch { consumed: i }
855	        }
856	    }

858	    #[inline(always)]
859	    fn read_record_dfa(
860	        &mut self,
861	        input: &[u8],
862	        output: &mut [u8],
863	        ends: &mut [usize],
864	    ) -> (ReadRecordResult, usize, usize, usize) {
865	        if input.is_empty() {
866	            let s = self.transition_final_dfa(self.dfa_state);
867	            let res =
868	                self.dfa.new_read_record_result(s, true, false, false, false);
869	            // This part is a little tricky. When reading the final record,
870	            // the last result the caller will get is an InputEmpty, and while
871	            // they'll have everything they need in `output`, they'll be
872	            // missing the final end position of the final field in `ends`.
873	            // We insert that here, but we must take care to handle the case
874	            // where `ends` doesn't have enough space. If it doesn't have
875	            // enough space, then we also can't transition to the next state.
876	            return match res {
877	                ReadRecordResult::Record => {
878	                    if ends.is_empty() {
879	                        return (ReadRecordResult::OutputEndsFull, 0, 0, 0);
880	                    }
881	                    self.dfa_state = s;
882	                    ends[0] = self.output_pos;
883	                    self.output_pos = 0;
884	                    (res, 0, 0, 1)
885	                }
886	                _ => {
887	                    self.dfa_state = s;
888	                    (res, 0, 0, 0)
889	                }
890	            };
891	        }
892	        if output.is_empty() {
893	            return (ReadRecordResult::OutputFull, 0, 0, 0);
894	        }
895	        if ends.is_empty() {
896	            return (ReadRecordResult::OutputEndsFull, 0, 0, 0);
897	        }
898	        let (mut nin, mut nout, mut nend) = (0, 0, 0);
899	        let mut state = self.dfa_state;
900	        while nin < input.len() && nout < output.len() && nend < ends.len() {
901	            let (s, has_out) = self.dfa.get_output(state, input[nin]);
902	            self.line += (input[nin] == b'\n') as u64;
903	            state = s;
904	            if has_out {
905	                output[nout] = input[nin];
906	                nout += 1;
907	            }
908	            nin += 1;
909	            if state >= self.dfa.final_field {
910	                ends[nend] = self.output_pos + nout;
911	                nend += 1;
912	                if state > self.dfa.final_field {
913	                    break;
914	                }
915	            }
916	            if state == self.dfa.in_field || state == self.dfa.in_quoted {
917	                self.dfa
918	                    .classes
919	                    .scan_and_copy(input, &mut nin, output, &mut nout);
920	            }
921	        }
922	        let res = self.dfa.new_read_record_result(
923	            state,
924	            false,
925	            nin >= input.len(),
926	            nout >= output.len(),
927	            nend >= ends.len(),
928	        );
929	        self.dfa_state = state;
930	        if res.is_record() {
931	            self.output_pos = 0;
932	        } else {
933	            self.output_pos += nout;
934	        }
935	        (res, nin, nout, nend)
936	    }

938	    #[inline(always)]
939	    fn read_field_dfa(
940	        &mut self,
941	        input: &[u8],
942	        output: &mut [u8],
943	    ) -> (ReadFieldResult, usize, usize) {
944	        if input.is_empty() {
945	            self.dfa_state = self.transition_final_dfa(self.dfa_state);
946	            let res = self.dfa.new_read_field_result(
947	                self.dfa_state,
948	                true,
949	                false,
950	                false,
951	            );
952	            return (res, 0, 0);
953	        }
954	        if output.is_empty() {
955	            return (ReadFieldResult::OutputFull, 0, 0);
956	        }
957	        let (mut nin, mut nout) = (0, 0);
958	        let mut state = self.dfa_state;
959	        while nin < input.len() && nout < output.len() {
960	            let b = input[nin];
961	            self.line += (b == b'\n') as u64;
962	            let (s, has_out) = self.dfa.get_output(state, b);
963	            state = s;
964	            if has_out {
965	                output[nout] = b;
966	                nout += 1;
967	            }
968	            nin += 1;
969	            if state >= self.dfa.final_field {
970	                break;
971	            }
972	        }
973	        let res = self.dfa.new_read_field_result(
974	            state,
975	            false,
976	            nin >= input.len(),
977	            nout >= output.len(),
978	        );
979	        self.dfa_state = state;
980	        (res, nin, nout)
981	    }

983	    /// Perform the final state transition, i.e., when the caller indicates
984	    /// that the input has been exhausted.
985	    fn transition_final_dfa(&self, state: DfaState) -> DfaState {
986	        // If we''ve already emitted a record or think we're ready to start
987	        // parsing a new record, then we should sink into the final state
988	        // and never move from there. (pro-tip: the start state doubles as
989	        // the final state!)
990	        if state >= self.dfa.final_record || state.is_start() {
991	            self.dfa.new_state_final_end()
992	        } else {
993	            self.dfa.new_state_final_record()
994	        }
995	    }

997	    /// Write the transition tables for the DFA based on this parser's
998	    /// configuration.
999	    fn build_dfa(&mut self) {
1000	        // A naive DFA transition table has
1001	        // `cells = (# number of states) * (# size of alphabet)`. While we
1002	        // could get away with that, the table would have `10 * 256 = 2560`
1003	        // entries. Even worse, in order to avoid a multiplication instruction
1004	        // when computing the next transition, we store the starting index of
1005	        // each state's row, which would not be representible in a single byte.
1006	        // So we'd need a `u16`, which doubles our transition table size to
1007	        // ~5KB. This is a lot to put on the stack, even though it probably
1008	        // fits in the L1 cache of most modern CPUs.
1009	        //
1010	        // To avoid this, we note that while our "true" alphabet
1011	        // has 256 distinct possibilities, the DFA itself is only
1012	        // discriminatory on a very small subset of that alphabet. For
1013	        // example, assuming neither `a` nor `b` are set as special
1014	        // quote/comment/escape/delimiter/terminator bytes, they are otherwise
1015	        // indistinguishable to the DFA, so it would be OK to treat them as
1016	        // if they were equivalent. That is, they are in the same equivalence
1017	        // class.
1018	        //
1019	        // As it turns out, using this logic, we can shrink our effective
1020	        // alphabet down to 7 equivalence classes:
1021	        //
1022	        //   1. The field delimiter.
1023	        //   2. The record terminator.
1024	        //   3. If the record terminator is CRLF, then CR and LF are
1025	        //      distinct equivalence classes.
1026	        //   4. The quote byte.
1027	        //   5. The escape byte.
1028	        //   6. The comment byte.
1029	        //   7. Everything else.
1030	        //
1031	        // We add those equivalence classes here. If more configuration knobs
1032	        // are added to the parser with more discriminating bytes, then this
1033	        // logic will need to be adjusted further.
1034	        //
1035	        // Even though this requires an extra bit of indirection when computing
1036	        // the next transition, microbenchmarks say that it doesn't make much
1037	        // of a difference. Perhaps because everything fits into the L1 cache.
1038	        self.dfa.classes.add(self.delimiter);
1039	        if self.quoting {
1040	            self.dfa.classes.add(self.quote);
1041	            if let Some(escape) = self.escape {
1042	                self.dfa.classes.add(escape);
1043	            }
1044	        }
1045	        if let Some(comment) = self.comment {
1046	            self.dfa.classes.add(comment);
1047	        }
1048	        match self.term {
1049	            Terminator::Any(b) => self.dfa.classes.add(b),
1050	            Terminator::CRLF => {
1051	                self.dfa.classes.add(b'\r');
1052	                self.dfa.classes.add(b'\n');
1053	            }
1054	        }
1055	        // Build the DFA transition table by computing the DFA state for all
1056	        // possible combinations of state and input byte.
1057	        for &state in NFA_STATES {
1058	            for c in (0..256).map(|c| c as u8) {
1059	                let mut nfa_result = (state, NfaInputAction::Epsilon);
1060	                // Consume NFA states until we hit a non-epsilon transition.
1061	                while nfa_result.0 != NfaState::End
1062	                    && nfa_result.1 == NfaInputAction::Epsilon
1063	                {
1064	                    nfa_result = self.transition_nfa(nfa_result.0, c);
1065	                }
1066	                let from = self.dfa.new_state(state);
1067	                let to = self.dfa.new_state(nfa_result.0);
1068	                self.dfa.set(
1069	                    from,
1070	                    c,
1071	                    to,
1072	                    nfa_result.1 == NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput,
1073	                );
1074	            }
1075	        }
1076	        self.dfa_state = self.dfa.new_state(NfaState::StartRecord);
1077	        self.dfa.finish();
1078	    }

1080	    // The NFA implementation follows. The transition_final_nfa and
1081	    // transition_nfa methods are required for the DFA to operate. The
1082	    // rest are included for completeness (and debugging). Note that this
1083	    // NFA implementation is included in most of the CSV parser tests below.
1084	
1085	    #[inline(always)]
1086	    fn read_record_nfa(
1087	        &mut self,
1088	        input: &[u8],
1089	        output: &mut [u8],
1090	        ends: &mut [usize],
1091	    ) -> (ReadRecordResult, usize, usize, usize) {
1092	        if input.is_empty() {
1093	            let s = self.transition_final_nfa(self.nfa_state);
1094	            let res = ReadRecordResult::from_nfa(s, false, false, false);
1095	            return match res {
1096	                ReadRecordResult::Record => {
1097	                    if ends.is_empty() {
1098	                        return (ReadRecordResult::OutputEndsFull, 0, 0, 0);
1099	                    }
1100	                    self.nfa_state = s;
1101	                    ends[0] = self.output_pos;
1102	                    self.output_pos = 0;
1103	                    (res, 0, 0, 1)
1104	                }
1105	                _ => {
1106	                    self.nfa_state = s;
1107	                    (res, 0, 0, 0)
1108	                }
1109	            };
1110	        }
1111	        if output.is_empty() {
1112	            return (ReadRecordResult::OutputFull, 0, 0, 0);
1113	        }
1114	        if ends.is_empty() {
1115	            return (ReadRecordResult::OutputEndsFull, 0, 0, 0);
1116	        }
1117	        let (mut nin, mut nout, mut nend) = (0, 0, 0);
1118	        let mut state = self.nfa_state;
1119	        while nin < input.len() && nout < output.len() && nend < ends.len() {
1120	            let (s, io) = self.transition_nfa(state, input[nin]);
1121	            match io {
1122	                NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput => {
1123	                    output[nout] = input[nin];
1124	                    nout += 1;
1125	                    nin += 1;
1126	                }
1127	                NfaInputAction::Discard => {
1128	                    nin += 1;
1129	                }
1130	                NfaInputAction::Epsilon => {}
1131	            }
1132	            state = s;
1133	            if state.is_field_final() {
1134	                ends[nend] = self.output_pos + nout;
1135	                nend += 1;
1136	                if state != NfaState::EndFieldDelim {
1137	                    break;
1138	                }
1139	            }
1140	        }
1141	        let res = ReadRecordResult::from_nfa(
1142	            state,
1143	            nin >= input.len(),
1144	            nout >= output.len(),
1145	            nend >= ends.len(),
1146	        );
1147	        self.nfa_state = state;
1148	        self.output_pos =
1149	            if res.is_record() { 0 } else { self.output_pos + nout };
1150	        (res, nin, nout, nend)
1151	    }

1153	    #[inline(always)]
1154	    fn read_field_nfa(
1155	        &mut self,
1156	        input: &[u8],
1157	        output: &mut [u8],
1158	    ) -> (ReadFieldResult, usize, usize) {
1159	        if input.is_empty() {
1160	            self.nfa_state = self.transition_final_nfa(self.nfa_state);
1161	            let res = ReadFieldResult::from_nfa(self.nfa_state, false, false);
1162	            return (res, 0, 0);
1163	        }
1164	        if output.is_empty() {
1165	            // If the output buffer is empty, then we can never make progress,
1166	            // so just quit now.
1167	            return (ReadFieldResult::OutputFull, 0, 0);
1168	        }
1169	        let (mut nin, mut nout) = (0, 0);
1170	        let mut state = self.nfa_state;
1171	        while nin < input.len() && nout < output.len() {
1172	            let (s, io) = self.transition_nfa(state, input[nin]);
1173	            match io {
1174	                NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput => {
1175	                    output[nout] = input[nin];
1176	                    nout += 1;
1177	                    nin += 1;
1178	                }
1179	                NfaInputAction::Discard => {
1180	                    nin += 1;
1181	                }
1182	                NfaInputAction::Epsilon => (),
1183	            }
1184	            state = s;
1185	            if state.is_field_final() {
1186	                break;
1187	            }
1188	        }
1189	        let res = ReadFieldResult::from_nfa(
1190	            state,
1191	            nin >= input.len(),
1192	            nout >= output.len(),
1193	        );
1194	        self.nfa_state = state;
1195	        (res, nin, nout)
1196	    }

1198	    /// Compute the final NFA transition after all caller-provided input has
1199	    /// been exhausted.
1200	    #[inline(always)]
1201	    fn transition_final_nfa(&self, state: NfaState) -> NfaState {
1202	        use self::NfaState::*;
1203	        match state {
1204	            End | StartRecord | EndRecord | InComment | CRLF => End,
1205	            StartField | EndFieldDelim | EndFieldTerm | InField
1206	            | InQuotedField | InEscapedQuote | InDoubleEscapedQuote
1207	            | InRecordTerm => EndRecord,
1208	        }
1209	    }
1210	
1211	    /// Compute the next NFA state given the current NFA state and the current
1212	    /// input byte.
1213	    ///
1214	    /// This returns the next NFA state along with an NfaInputAction that
1215	    /// indicates what should be done with the input byte (nothing for an epsilon
1216	    /// transition, copied to a caller provided output buffer, or discarded).
1217	    #[inline(always)]
1218	    fn transition_nfa(
1219	        &self,
1220	        state: NfaState,
1221	        c: u8,
1222	    ) -> (NfaState, NfaInputAction) {
1223	        use self::NfaState::*;
1224	        match state {
1225	            End => (End, NfaInputAction::Epsilon),
1226	            StartRecord => {
1227	                if self.term.equals(c) {
1228	                    (StartRecord, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1229	                } else if self.comment == Some(c) {
1230	                    (InComment, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1231	                } else {
1232	                    (StartField, NfaInputAction::Epsilon)
1233	                }
1234	            }
1235	            EndRecord => (StartRecord, NfaInputAction::Epsilon),
1236	            StartField => {
1237	                if self.quoting && self.quote == c {
1238	                    (InQuotedField, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1239	                } else if self.delimiter == c {
1240	                    (EndFieldDelim, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1241	                } else if self.term.equals(c) {
1242	                    (EndFieldTerm, NfaInputAction::Epsilon)
1243	                } else {
1244	                    (InField, NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput)
1245	                }
1246	            }
1247	            EndFieldDelim => (StartField, NfaInputAction::Epsilon),
1248	            EndFieldTerm => (InRecordTerm, NfaInputAction::Epsilon),
1249	            InField => {
1250	                if self.delimiter == c {
1251	                    (EndFieldDelim, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1252	                } else if self.term.equals(c) {
1253	                    (EndFieldTerm, NfaInputAction::Epsilon)
1254	                } else {
1255	                    (InField, NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput)
1256	                }
1257	            }
1258	            InQuotedField => {
1259	                if self.quoting && self.quote == c {
1260	                    (InDoubleEscapedQuote, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1261	                } else if self.quoting && self.escape == Some(c) {
1262	                    (InEscapedQuote, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1263	                } else {
1264	                    (InQuotedField, NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput)
1265	                }
1266	            }
1267	            InEscapedQuote => (InQuotedField, NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput),
1268	            InDoubleEscapedQuote => {
1269	                if self.quoting && self.double_quote && self.quote == c {
1270	                    (InQuotedField, NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput)
1271	                } else if self.delimiter == c {
1272	                    (EndFieldDelim, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1273	                } else if self.term.equals(c) {
1274	                    (EndFieldTerm, NfaInputAction::Epsilon)
1275	                } else {
1276	                    (InField, NfaInputAction::CopyToOutput)
1277	                }
1278	            }
1279	            InComment => {
1280	                if b'\n' == c {
1281	                    (StartRecord, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1282	                } else {
1283	                    (InComment, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1284	                }
1285	            }
1286	            InRecordTerm => {
1287	                if self.term.is_crlf() && b'\r' == c {
1288	                    (CRLF, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1289	                } else {
1290	                    (EndRecord, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1291	                }
1292	            }
1293	            CRLF => {
1294	                if b'\n' == c {
1295	                    (StartRecord, NfaInputAction::Discard)
1296	                } else {
1297	                    (StartRecord, NfaInputAction::Epsilon)
1298	                }
1299	            }
1300	        }
1301	    }

1304	/// The number of slots in the DFA transition table.
1305	///
1306	/// This number is computed by multiplying the maximum number of transition
1307	/// classes (7) by the total number of NFA states that are used in the DFA
1308	/// (10).
1309	///
1310	/// The number of transition classes is determined by an equivalence class of
1311	/// bytes, where every byte in the same equivalence classes is
1312	/// indistinguishable from any other byte with respect to the DFA. For example,
1313	/// if neither `a` nor `b` are specifed as a delimiter/quote/terminator/escape,
1314	/// then the DFA will never discriminate between `a` or `b`, so they can
1315	/// effectively be treated as identical. This reduces storage space
1316	/// substantially.
1317	///
1318	/// The total number of NFA states (13) is greater than the total number of
1319	/// NFA states that are in the DFA. In particular, any NFA state that can only
1320	/// be reached by epsilon transitions will never have explicit usage in the
1321	/// DFA.
1322	const TRANS_CLASSES: usize = 7;
1323	const DFA_STATES: usize = 10;
1324	const TRANS_SIZE: usize = TRANS_CLASSES * DFA_STATES;
1325	
1326	/// The number of possible transition classes. (See the comment on `TRANS_SIZE`
1327	/// for more details.)
1328	const CLASS_SIZE: usize = 256;
1329	
1330	/// A representation of a DFA.
1331	///
1332	/// For the most part, this is a transition table, but various optimizations
1333	/// have been applied to reduce its memory footprint.
1334	struct Dfa {
1335	    /// The core transition table. Each row corresponds to the transitions for
1336	    /// each input equivalence class. (Input bytes are mapped to their
1337	    /// corresponding equivalence class with the `classes` map.)
1338	    ///
1339	    /// DFA states are represented as an index corresponding to the start of
1340	    /// its row in this table.
1341	    trans: [DfaState; TRANS_SIZE],
1342	    /// A table with the same layout as `trans`, except its values indicate
1343	    /// whether a particular `(state, equivalence class)` pair should emit an
1344	    /// output byte.
1345	    has_output: [bool; TRANS_SIZE],
1346	    /// A map from input byte to equivalence class.
1347	    ///
1348	    /// This is responsible for reducing the effective alphabet size from
1349	    /// 256 to `TRANS_CLASSES`.
1350	    classes: DfaClasses,
1351	    /// The DFA state corresponding to being inside an unquoted field.
1352	    in_field: DfaState,
1353	    /// The DFA state corresponding to being inside an quoted field.
1354	    in_quoted: DfaState,
1355	    /// The minimum DFA state that indicates a field has been parsed. All DFA
1356	    /// states greater than this are also final-field states.
1357	    final_field: DfaState,
1358	    /// The minimum DFA state that indicates a record has been parsed. All DFA
1359	    /// states greater than this are also final-record states.
1360	    final_record: DfaState,
1361	}
1362	
1363	impl Dfa {
1364	    fn new() -> Dfa {
1365	        Dfa {
1366	            trans: [DfaState(0); TRANS_SIZE],
1367	            has_output: [false; TRANS_SIZE],
1368	            classes: DfaClasses::new(),
1369	            in_field: DfaState(0),
1370	            in_quoted: DfaState(0),
1371	            final_field: DfaState(0),
1372	            final_record: DfaState(0),
1373	        }
1374	    }
1375	
1376	    fn new_state(&self, nfa_state: NfaState) -> DfaState {
1377	        let nclasses = self.classes.num_classes() as u8;
1378	        let idx = (nfa_state as u8).checked_mul(nclasses).unwrap();
1379	        DfaState(idx)
1380	    }
1381	
1382	    fn new_state_final_end(&self) -> DfaState {
1383	        self.new_state(NfaState::StartRecord)
1384	    }
1385	
1386	    fn new_state_final_record(&self) -> DfaState {
1387	        self.new_state(NfaState::EndRecord)
1388	    }
1389	
1390	    fn get_output(&self, state: DfaState, c: u8) -> (DfaState, bool) {
1391	        let cls = self.classes.classes[c as usize];
1392	        let idx = state.0 as usize + cls as usize;
1393	        (self.trans[idx], self.has_output[idx])
1394	    }
1395	
1396	    fn set(&mut self, from: DfaState, c: u8, to: DfaState, output: bool) {
1397	        let cls = self.classes.classes[c as usize];
1398	        let idx = from.0 as usize + cls as usize;
1399	        self.trans[idx] = to;
1400	        self.has_output[idx] = output;
1401	    }
1402	
1403	    fn finish(&mut self) {
1404	        self.in_field = self.new_state(NfaState::InField);
1405	        self.in_quoted = self.new_state(NfaState::InQuotedField);
1406	        self.final_field = self.new_state(NfaState::EndFieldDelim);
1407	        self.final_record = self.new_state(NfaState::EndRecord);
1408	    }
1409	
1410	    fn new_read_field_result(
1411	        &self,
1412	        state: DfaState,
1413	        is_final_trans: bool,
1414	        inpdone: bool,
1415	        outdone: bool,
1416	    ) -> ReadFieldResult {
1417	        if state >= self.final_record {
1418	            ReadFieldResult::Field { record_end: true }
1419	        } else if state == self.final_field {
1420	            ReadFieldResult::Field { record_end: false }
1421	        } else if is_final_trans && state.is_start() {
1422	            ReadFieldResult::End
1423	        } else {
1424	            debug_assert!(state < self.final_field);
1425	            if !inpdone && outdone {
1426	                ReadFieldResult::OutputFull
1427	            } else {
1428	                ReadFieldResult::InputEmpty
1429	            }
1430	        }
1431	    }
1432	
1433	    fn new_read_record_result(
1434	        &self,
1435	        state: DfaState,
1436	        is_final_trans: bool,
1437	        inpdone: bool,
1438	        outdone: bool,
1439	        endsdone: bool,
1440	    ) -> ReadRecordResult {
1441	        if state >= self.final_record {
1442	            ReadRecordResult::Record
1443	        } else if is_final_trans && state.is_start() {
1444	            ReadRecordResult::End
1445	        } else {
1446	            debug_assert!(state < self.final_record);
1447	            if !inpdone && outdone {
1448	                ReadRecordResult::OutputFull
1449	            } else if !inpdone && endsdone {
1450	                ReadRecordResult::OutputEndsFull
1451	            } else {
1452	                ReadRecordResult::InputEmpty
1453	            }
1454	        }
1455	    }
1456	}

1458	/// A map from input byte to equivalence class.
1459	struct DfaClasses {
1460	    classes: [u8; CLASS_SIZE],
1461	    next_class: usize,
1462	}
1463	
1464	impl DfaClasses {
1465	    fn new() -> DfaClasses {
1466	        DfaClasses { classes: [0; CLASS_SIZE], next_class: 1 }
1467	    }
1468	
1469	    fn add(&mut self, b: u8) {
1470	        if self.next_class > CLASS_SIZE {
1471	            panic!("added too many classes")
1472	        }
1473	        self.classes[b as usize] = self.next_class as u8;
1474	        self.next_class += 1;
1475	    }
1476	
1477	    fn num_classes(&self) -> usize {
1478	        self.next_class
1479	    }
1480	
1481	    /// Scan and copy the input bytes to the output buffer quickly.
1482	    ///
1483	    /// This assumes that the current state of the DFA is either `InField` or
1484	    /// `InQuotedField`. In this case, all bytes corresponding to the first
1485	    /// equivalence class (i.e., not a delimiter/quote/escape/etc.) are
1486	    /// guaranteed to never result in a state transition out of the current
1487	    /// state. This function takes advantage of that copies every byte from
1488	    /// `input` in the first equivalence class to `output`. Once a byte is seen
1489	    /// outside the first equivalence class, we quit and should fall back to
1490	    /// the main DFA loop.
1491	    #[inline(always)]
1492	    fn scan_and_copy(
1493	        &self,
1494	        input: &[u8],
1495	        nin: &mut usize,
1496	        output: &mut [u8],
1497	        nout: &mut usize,
1498	    ) {
1499	        while *nin < input.len()
1500	            && *nout < output.len()
1501	            && self.classes[input[*nin] as usize] == 0
1502	        {
1503	            output[*nout] = input[*nin];
1504	            *nin += 1;
1505	            *nout += 1;
1506	        }
1507	    }
1508	}

1510	/// A single DFA state.
1511	///
1512	/// A DFA state is represented by the starting index of its corresponding row
1513	/// in the DFA transition table. This representation allows us to elide a
1514	/// single multiplication instruction when computing the next transition for
1515	/// a particular input byte.
1516	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, Ord, PartialEq, PartialOrd)]
1517	struct DfaState(u8);
1518	
1519	impl DfaState {
1520	    fn start() -> DfaState {
1521	        DfaState(0)
1522	    }
1523	
1524	    fn is_start(&self) -> bool {
1525	        self.0 == 0
1526	    }
1527	}

1636	    fn parse_by_field(rdr: &mut Reader, data: &str) -> Csv {
1637	        let mut data = data.as_bytes();
1638	        let mut field = [0u8; 10];
1639	        let mut csv = Csv::new();
1640	        let mut row = Row::new();
1641	        let mut outpos = 0;
1642	        loop {
1643	            let (res, nin, nout) = rdr.read_field(data, &mut field[outpos..]);
1644	            data = &data[nin..];
1645	            outpos += nout;
1646	
1647	            match res {
1648	                ReadFieldResult::InputEmpty => {
1649	                    if !data.is_empty() {
1650	                        panic!("missing input data")
1651	                    }
1652	                }
1653	                ReadFieldResult::OutputFull => panic!("field too large"),
1654	                ReadFieldResult::Field { record_end } => {
1655	                    let s = str::from_utf8(&field[..outpos]).unwrap();
1656	                    row.push(Field::from(s).unwrap());
1657	                    outpos = 0;
1658	                    if record_end {
1659	                        csv.push(row);
1660	                        row = Row::new();
1661	                    }
1662	                }
1663	                ReadFieldResult::End => {
1664	                    return csv;
1665	                }
1666	            }
1667	        }
1668	    }

1673	        let mut data = data.as_bytes();
1674	        let mut record = [0; 1024];
1675	        let mut ends = [0; 10];
1676	
1677	        let mut csv = Csv::new();
1678	        let (mut outpos, mut endpos) = (0, 0);
1679	        loop {
1680	            let (res, nin, nout, nend) = rdr.read_record(
1681	                data,
1682	                &mut record[outpos..],
1683	                &mut ends[endpos..],
1684	            );
1685	            data = &data[nin..];
1686	            outpos += nout;
1687	            endpos += nend;
1688	
1689	            match res {
1690	                InputEmpty => {
1691	                    if !data.is_empty() {
1692	                        panic!("missing input data")
1693	                    }
1694	                }
1695	                OutputFull => panic!("record too large (out buffer)"),
1696	                OutputEndsFull => panic!("record too large (end buffer)"),
1697	                Record => {
1698	                    let s = str::from_utf8(&record[..outpos]).unwrap();
1699	                    let mut start = 0;

1701	                    for &end in &ends[..endpos] {
1702	                        row.push(Field::from(&s[start..end]).unwrap());

1707	                    endpos = 0;
1708	                }

1710	            }

All 10 test suites pass and the `no-default-features` check is clean. The implementation is complete.

## 实现总结

在 `src/reader.rs` 和 `src/string_record.rs` 中实现了可选启用的"暂时无数据后继续读取"功能（未启用时行为完全不变）：

**API（`ReaderBuilder`）**
- 新增 `continue_on_would_block(bool)`（默认关闭），并附 `would_block_continue` / `retry_on_would_block` / `resume_on_would_block` 三个别名，均带文档和可运行的 doc 示例。

**核心机制（`src/reader.rs`）**
- `ReaderState` 新增 `pending: Option<PendingRecord>`：`WouldBlock` 发生时，把已读出的部分记录（字段缓冲区、字段结束位置、记录起点 `Position`）暂存到 **Reader 内部**（而非调用方的记录对象），然后原样返回 `Some(Err(WouldBlock))`；不设置 EOF，`is_done()` 保持 `false`，当前调用立即返回。
- 下一次 `read_byte_record_impl` 先把暂存内容恢复到调用方传入的任意记录对象中再继续解析——因此换记录对象、字节读取切换到字符串读取、丢弃借用迭代器后重建，都不会丢失暂停中的内容。暂存时保留完整缓冲区容量，避免恢复后缓冲区收缩导致解析器在 `OutputEndsFull` 上反复打转（这是调试中发现并修复的一个真实活锁）。
- 底层解析状态（DFA 状态、BOM 检测、行号、`output_pos`）本就在 `CoreReader` 中持久，因此 BOM 未收齐、引号字段内换行/成对引号、CRLF 之间、多字节字符（如中文）中间暂停都能正确续读；真正返回 0 字节才走原有 EOF 规则，无行尾的最后一条记录仍只交付一次；其他 I/O 错误保持"停止读取"行为；`seek`/`seek_raw` 会丢弃未完成的暂存记录。

**表头与 Serde**
- 表头读取遇 `WouldBlock` 时错误直接传播、不缓存半条表头；两个 deserialize 迭代器在 `next()` 中通过 `retry_headers` 重试表头解析：遇 `WouldBlock` 交付该错误，取得完整表头后按名称映射（不会退回按列次序映射），表头仍不作为数据记录返回；其他表头错误保持原有的位置映射回退行为。

**UTF-8（`src/string_record.rs`）**
- 暂停中未收齐的字符不会被报成 UTF-8 错误（出错时记录已清空，校验在完整记录到达后才进行）；完整记录确实含无效 UTF-8 时，UTF-8 错误的记录位置改从记录对象自身获取（续读时 reader 的当前位置已越过记录起点），字段编号、字段内偏移和记录位置与不中断读取完全一致，字节接口仍保留原始字节。

**测试**：新增 8 个单元测试，用 `Stutter`（每交付 1 字节前暂停 N 次的 `Read` 实现）覆盖：未启用时的兼容停止行为、逐字节+暂停与不中断读取的字段/Position 一致性（含 BOM、引号内 CRLF、成对引号、中文、无行尾末记录）、连续多次暂停、更换记录对象与字节/字符串切换、无效 UTF-8 的字节/字符串两种接口行为、表头暂停下的 Serde 名称映射（借用与所有权迭代器）、借用迭代器丢弃重建、字段数检查位置兼容、空输入与 EOF 粘性。全部 150 个 lib 测试及整个 workspace（含 doc 测试、csv-core、csv-index、BOM 验收测试）通过，`cargo fmt` 已应用、`cargo doc` 无警告。
